items.title: Buried in Meta’s $18B settlement is a legal pass on kids’ data
items.feed_excerpt: Meta’s settlement with 29 states allows it to retain certain data from children under 13 to train and test age-detection models, highlighting a privacy tradeoff built into the deal.

items.title: YouTube now lets creators tag Amazon products and earn commissions from purchases
items.feed_excerpt: The update turns product recommendations into a more direct revenue stream for creators, and for Amazon, the move puts its massive online marketplace inside one of the most popular video platforms.

items.title: Barret Zoph, the Thinking Machines co-founder who defected to OpenAI, is now at Google
items.feed_excerpt: Zoph, who co-founded Thinking Machines Lab alongside Mira Murati and also served as the startup's CTO, led a brief stint at OpenAI and is now at Google.

items.title: Hoomanely’s building a smart feeding bowl and an AI platform to help owners spot when their pup is sick
items.feed_excerpt: Hoomanely has developed a smart bowl to measure and record dogs' feeding data, then tells owners if behaviors change.

items.title: Google’s AI Mode can now track flight prices, help book hotels, and more
items.feed_excerpt: The updates indicate that Google is looking to position AI Mode as an AI travel agent of sorts, as it's moving beyond simply helping users find information to actually handling parts of the trip-planning and booking process.

items.title: This former PG&E engineer is building a ‘Google Maps for the underground’
items.feed_excerpt: The startup just raised a $26 million Series A to grow its customer base and help reduce red tape for utility and construction work.

items.title: Hugging Face is selling a cute $399 open source duck robot, Microduck
items.feed_excerpt: Clem Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face, said the Microduck is an “open-source robot you can teach new tricks with reinforcement learning.”

items.title: Hold up, there’s a new Twitter in town
items.feed_excerpt: Former Twitter trademark counsel Stephen Coates said in a LinkedIn post that the company is not trying to re-create Twitter.

items.title: Sprains, pain, and whiplash: Waymo and Zoox test drivers are getting hurt as robotaxis scale
items.feed_excerpt: Test drivers for Waymo and Zoox sustained more than two dozen injuries in 2024 and 2025 from hard braking or other sudden movements made by the autonomous vehicles, according to a TechCrunch review of data submitted to OSHA.

items.title: Australian police arrest two over TeamPCP hacks targeting Mercor, OpenAI, and others
items.feed_excerpt: The arrests come after a wave of cyberattacks earlier this year targeting tech companies that rely on high-profile and widely used open source software.

items.title: AI’s memory crunch is coming for Android apps
items.feed_excerpt: Google is setting new memory-use limits for Android apps as AI data centers contribute to hardware shortages that could leave lower-cost phones with less memory.

items.title: Here’s all the times AI has gone rogue and hacked other companies
items.feed_excerpt: A recap of all the incidents involving LLMs made by Anthropic, Meta, and OpenAI, which went rogue and attacked real companies and individuals on the internet.

items.title: Plaud’s new earphones come with an eSIM-enabled case for talking to AI agents
items.feed_excerpt: Plaud's new 'agentic' earbuds are priced at $249.

items.title: OpenAI to start showing ads on ChatGPT’s free and Go tiers in India
items.feed_excerpt: OpenAI has more than 100 million weekly active ChatGPT users in India, a huge chunk of whom are on the free or the lower-priced Go tiers.

items.title: Nvidia closes in on Hugging Face acquisition
items.feed_excerpt: Nvidia has reportedly agreed to buy Hugging Face, the popular open source AI hub, for $12.9 billion in a move that would let Nvidia both protect its chip empire and jump back into the cloud business.
